The right angle is at S, so the side opposite it, TU, is the hypotenuse. By Pythagoras' theorem, \(TU^{2} = TS^{2} + SU^{2} = 5^{2} + 12^{2} = 25 + 144 = 169\), so \(TU = 13\).
For \(\angle T\): the opposite side is SU = 12, the adjacent side is TS = 5, the hypotenuse is TU = 13.
\(\sin T = \frac{SU}{TU} = \frac{12}{13}\), \(\cos T = \frac{TS}{TU} = \frac{5}{13}\), \(\tan T = \frac{SU}{TS} = \frac{12}{5}\).
For \(\angle U\): the opposite side is TS = 5, the adjacent side is SU = 12, the hypotenuse is TU = 13.
\(\sin U = \frac{TS}{TU} = \frac{5}{13}\), \(\cos U = \frac{SU}{TU} = \frac{12}{13}\), \(\tan U = \frac{TS}{SU} = \frac{5}{12}\).
So \(\sin T = \frac{12}{13},\ \cos T = \frac{5}{13},\ \tan T = \frac{12}{5}\) and \(\sin U = \frac{5}{13},\ \cos U = \frac{12}{13},\ \tan U = \frac{5}{12}\).

The right angle is at X, so the side opposite it, YZ = 17 cm, is the hypotenuse, and XZ = 8 cm, XY are the two legs. By Pythagoras' theorem, \(XY^{2} = YZ^{2} - XZ^{2} = 17^{2} - 8^{2} = 289 - 64 = 225\), so \(XY = 15\) cm.
For \(\angle Y\): the opposite side is XZ = 8, the adjacent side is XY = 15, the hypotenuse is YZ = 17.
\(\sin Y = \frac{XZ}{YZ} = \frac{8}{17}\), \(\cos Y = \frac{XY}{YZ} = \frac{15}{17}\), \(\tan Y = \frac{XZ}{XY} = \frac{8}{15}\).
For \(\angle Z\): the opposite side is XY = 15, the adjacent side is XZ = 8, the hypotenuse is YZ = 17.
\(\sin Z = \frac{XY}{YZ} = \frac{15}{17}\), \(\cos Z = \frac{XZ}{YZ} = \frac{8}{17}\), \(\tan Z = \frac{XY}{XZ} = \frac{15}{8}\).
So \(\sin Y = \frac{8}{17},\ \cos Y = \frac{15}{17},\ \tan Y = \frac{8}{15}\) and \(\sin Z = \frac{15}{17},\ \cos Z = \frac{8}{17},\ \tan Z = \frac{15}{8}\).

\(\angle M = 90^{\circ}\), so LN is the hypotenuse and \(\theta = \angle N\) is an acute angle of the triangle.
Use \(\sin^{2} \theta + \cos^{2} \theta = 1\): \(\sin^{2} \theta = 1 - \cos^{2} \theta = 1 - \left(\frac{24}{25}\right)^{2} = 1 - \frac{576}{625} = \frac{49}{625}\).
Since \(\theta\) is acute, \(\sin \theta\) is positive, so \(\sin \theta = \sqrt{\frac{49}{625}} = \frac{7}{25}\).
Then \(\tan \theta = \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} = \frac{7/25}{24/25} = \frac{7}{24}\).
Also \(\cos^{2} \theta = \left(\frac{24}{25}\right)^{2} = \frac{576}{625}\).
So \(\sin \theta = \frac{7}{25},\ \tan \theta = \frac{7}{24},\ \sin^{2} \theta = \frac{49}{625},\ \cos^{2} \theta = \frac{576}{625}\).

In a right angled triangle the two acute angles are complementary, and the side opposite one is the side adjacent to the other, so \(\sin \theta = \cos (90^{\circ} - \theta)\).
Taking \(\theta = 20^{\circ}\), \(\sin 20^{\circ} = \cos (90^{\circ} - 20^{\circ}) = \cos 70^{\circ}\).
The blank is \(70\), that is \(\sin 20^{\circ} = \cos 70^{\circ}\).

For an acute angle \(\theta\), \(\sin (90^{\circ} - \theta) = \cos \theta\) and \(\cos (90^{\circ} - \theta) = \sin \theta\), so \(\tan (90^{\circ} - \theta) = \frac{\sin (90^{\circ} - \theta)}{\cos (90^{\circ} - \theta)} = \frac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta}\).
Hence \(\tan \theta \times \tan (90^{\circ} - \theta) = \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} \times \frac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta} = 1\).
Taking \(\theta = 30^{\circ}\), the second angle is \(90^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}\); as a check, \(\tan 30^{\circ} \times \tan 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \times \sqrt{3} = 1\).
The blank is \(60\), that is \(\tan 30^{\circ} \times \tan 60^{\circ} = 1\).

For an acute angle \(\theta\), \(\cos \theta = \sin (90^{\circ} - \theta)\), since the side adjacent to \(\theta\) is the side opposite its complement.
Taking \(\theta = 40^{\circ}\), \(\cos 40^{\circ} = \sin (90^{\circ} - 40^{\circ}) = \sin 50^{\circ}\).
The blank is \(50\), that is \(\cos 40^{\circ} = \sin 50^{\circ}\).
